key_insight: In Fe-doped and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3(001), the OER activity is strongly controlled by defect charge state and Fermi level, making the overpotential a defect-chemistry property rather than a fixed surface property.
engineering_relevance: Fermi-level engineering can be used to predict and tune whether Fe dopants or oxygen vacancies preserve, worsen, or recover OER performance in perovskite oxide electrodes.
method: First-principles DFT for Fe dopants and oxygen vacancies in multiple charge states
Charge-dependent defect formation energies, segregation energies, and charge transition levels
Computational hydrogen electrode calculations of OER free-energy profiles
evidence_signal: The abstract reports overpotentials ranging from near-pristine values of 0.43–0.48 V to strongly degraded cases up to 2.13 V, depending on defect type, charge state, and adsorption site.
watch_item: Because the conclusions depend on calculated defect charge states and surface terminations, real materials may show additional effects from temperature, kinetics, and non-ideal surface reconstruction.
paper_title: Fermi-Level-Dependent Defect Chemistry and Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Fe-Doped and Oxygen-Deficient \ce{SrTiO3}(001)
